headline: RBA holds rates at 4.35% but warns hikes still on the table, while PLS surges 4.3% on strong lithium price recovery and Middle East shipping tensions push gold to record highs near US$4,470.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS was today's standout mover, jumping 4.3% in a strong session for lithium stocks. Albemarle (the world's biggest lithium producer) reported surging earnings on market recovery, and RBC flagged resilient demand — that kind of news lifts the whole lithium sector including Pilbara. Still well down from cost basis, but today's move is a genuine positive signal.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two slipped 1.2% last night despite overwhelmingly positive GTA VI headlines — pre-orders are reportedly at eye-watering levels and a Netflix exclusivity deal was defended by the CEO. The dip looks like broader tech sector caution rather than anything company-specific. The GTA VI story remains very much intact.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft edged down 0.4% last night in a soft session for the NASDAQ. There's no bad news here — analysts note the stock has cleared a key technical hurdle but still trails the broader S&P 500 year-to-date. The long-term AI growth story is unchanged.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI eased 0.5% today, tracking a soft session for tech-adjacent stocks on the ASX. No specific catalyst — mirrors the mild pullback across global AI-exposed equities. The ETF remains in the red overall, but the AI sector fundamentals remain strong with continued product launches from Google, Meta, and Anthropic this week.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE slipped 0.4% today in a quiet session. Emerging markets broadly tracked global risk-off sentiment amid Middle East shipping tensions and a slightly firmer US dollar. Singapore's upgraded growth forecast on AI tailwinds is a modest positive for the EM outlook.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG dipped a small 0.3% today, basically in line with the broader ASX 200 which fell 0.45%. Nothing to worry about — diversified funds move with the market and today's ASX softness was mild. Long-term picture unchanged.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS fell 0.3% today, reflecting last night's soft US session where the S&P 500 eased 0.3% and the NASDAQ dropped 0.6%. The Aussie-listed ETF tracks the whole US market, so it moves with Wall Street — this is a minor daily wobble, nothing more.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: No price data available for GOOG today — pricing can occasionally be delayed or unavailable. Alphabet's news flow is positive: earnings and cloud growth drove recent gains, and the company just launched Gemini 3.7 Flash this week. A new AI boss has been appointed to help close the gap with OpenAI and Anthropic.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX surges 4.3% — lithium recovery gaining momentum
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals had a standout session today, up 4.3% on the back of strong global lithium news — Albemarle's earnings surged and RBC flagged resilient demand. PLS is still well below your cost basis (down ~27.6% overall), but this is the kind of move that signals the sector may have found a floor. For a long-term holder, this is encouraging — sit tight and let the recovery play out.

watch_today.title: TTWO dip despite stellar GTA VI news — stay the course
watch_today.detail: Take-Two fell 1.2% last night even as GTA VI pre-orders hit 'eye-watering levels' and the CEO defended a high-profile Netflix exclusivity deal for an extended look at the game. The drop is broader market noise, not company-specific bad news. The GTA VI launch is shaping up to be a generational gaming event. Long-term case is very much intact — hold.

watch_today.title: RBA holds at 4.35% but hikes still possible — watch your mortgage
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank kept the cash rate on hold at 4.35% today as expected, but Governor Michele Bullock kept the door firmly open to further increases if inflation doesn't cooperate. This matters for your portfolio because higher rates for longer tend to weigh on growth stocks and property. Keep an eye on the next inflation data print — that'll determine the RBA's next move.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI ETF still underwater, but sector news is strong
watch_today.detail: Your Global X AI ETF is down 12.6% overall and slipped another 0.5% today. However, this week has seen a flurry of AI product launches — Google's Gemini 3.7 Flash, Anthropic's Claude for Teachers, and Meta's new open-source model. The underlying AI growth story is accelerating. For a long-term holder, this is a hold — the ETF just needs time for valuations to catch up to the hype.

watch_today.title: Gold hits near-record US$4,469 — Middle East tensions driving safe-haven demand
watch_today.detail: Gold surged almost 2% last night to near US$4,469 per ounce as shipping attacks in the Red Sea escalated and Iran war talks hit a fresh impasse. This is a classic 'fear trade' — investors buying gold when geopolitical risk spikes. Relevant for your portfolio as it signals ongoing global uncertainty that could weigh on risk assets like equities.

watch_today.title: MSFT steady — AI earnings week, nothing alarming
watch_today.detail: Microsoft dipped just 0.4% last night in a soft NASDAQ session. Analysts describe the question of 'what to do with Microsoft' as simple right now — the AI and cloud story remains strong. For a long-term holder, this is a hold. No new bad news, just a quiet night.

world.summary: The biggest global story today is escalating conflict in the Middle East, with shipping attacks in the Red Sea intensifying and Iran nuclear talks at an impasse. Separately, three regional powers have formed a new alliance, and a US judge has blocked Trump's mail voting restrictions.

stories.title: Shipping attacks escalate in Red Sea as Iran nuclear talks collapse
stories.why_it_matters: Houthi rebels in Yemen have resumed attacks on Red Sea shipping, and the US has struck a container ship in the Gulf of Oman — the death toll of sailors killed in the Red Sea has risen to four. Iran is also digging in on demands related to the Strait of Hormuz (a critical oil chokepoint), as nuclear talks hit a fresh impasse. This matters to everyday Australians because the Red Sea carries a huge chunk of global trade — disruptions push up shipping costs, which eventually show up in the price of goods you buy. It also pushed gold up nearly 2% last night as investors scrambled for safe havens.

stories.title: Three Middle East regional powers form new alliance amid ongoing war
stories.why_it_matters: Three regional powers in the Middle East have quietly signed a new alliance agreement, even as the broader conflict continues to reshape the region. The article doesn't name all parties explicitly, but the move signals that countries are recalibrating their strategic alliances as the US-Iran confrontation drags on. For Australia, this kind of geopolitical realignment can affect energy supply chains, defence posture in the Indo-Pacific, and the price of oil — which ticked up 0.9% last night to US$83.93 a barrel.

stories.title: US judge blocks Trump order limiting mail voting
stories.why_it_matters: A federal judge has blocked a Trump administration executive order that tried to restrict mail-in voting across the United States, ruling it overstepped presidential authority. Separately, the Department of Homeland Security is intensifying its hunt for non-citizens on voter rolls. With US mid-term elections approaching and major trade and geopolitical policy tied to who controls Congress, this legal battle over voting rights is one to watch — US political stability has direct knock-on effects for global markets including the ASX.

stories.title: Singapore upgrades 2026 growth forecast on AI boom and resilient global economy
stories.why_it_matters: Singapore has raised its official economic growth forecast for 2026, citing the AI technology boom and a more resilient-than-expected global economy as the main drivers. This is a broadly positive signal for Asia-Pacific markets, including Australia. Singapore is a key financial hub and bellwether for regional trade — when it upgrades its outlook, it tends to be a reliable indicator that conditions across Asia are improving. Good background news for your emerging markets holding (VGE.AX).

markets.summary: A soft night on Wall Street last night with the NASDAQ down 0.6% and the S&P 500 off 0.3%, while the ASX 200 closed today down 0.45% at 9,209. The standout moves were in commodities: gold surged nearly 2% to an extraordinary US$4,469 per ounce on Middle East fears, while oil ticked up 0.9% to US$83.93. The Aussie dollar held steady at US$0.706.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Closed down 0.45% today — mild weakness tracking soft global sentiment.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Fell 0.3% last night — modest pullback in a quiet session.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Down 0.6% last night — tech stocks leading the softness.

indicators.name: Gold (WTI)
indicators.note: Surged nearly 2% — Middle East conflict and shipping attacks driving safe-haven demand.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Up 0.9% — Red Sea shipping disruptions and Iran tensions supporting oil prices.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Essentially flat — the Aussie dollar is holding steady around 70.6 US cents.

politics.summary: The RBA dominated Australian news today, holding the cash rate at 4.35% but refusing to rule out further hikes. Meanwhile, Labor and the Coalition are edging toward a deal on VIP gambling perks, and Pauline Hanson made a move in the Senate that was shot down almost immediately.

stories.title: RBA holds cash rate at 4.35% — but threatens more hikes if needed
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia kept the official cash rate on hold at 4.35% today, as widely expected. But Governor Michele Bullock made clear that further rate increases remain firmly on the table if inflation doesn't keep falling. For everyday Australians, this means mortgage repayments stay high for the foreseeable future — there's no rate cut coming soon. For investors, higher-for-longer rates tend to put pressure on growth stocks and property valuations. The next key test is the next quarterly inflation print.

stories.title: Labor and Coalition edge toward deal on VIP gambling perks
stories.why_it_matters: The Labor government and the Coalition are reportedly close to a deal to crack down on VIP gambling perks — the kind of high-roller inducements that casinos and betting agencies offer their biggest-spending customers. This is part of the broader push for gambling reform following the Crown and Star casino scandals. A bipartisan deal would give the legislation a clear path through parliament, potentially reshaping how Australia's major casino and wagering operators do business.

stories.title: Pauline Hanson's Senate move shot down in 'under 30 seconds'
stories.why_it_matters: One Nation leader Pauline Hanson attempted a procedural move in the Senate today that was reportedly voted down in less than 30 seconds by other senators. While the specifics of the motion aren't fully detailed, it underscores how isolated One Nation remains in the upper house — their ability to influence legislation is limited without crossbench support. It's a reminder that the Senate's balance of power continues to shape what the Albanese government can and can't get done.

ai.summary: A big week for AI product launches — Google dropped Gemini 3.7 Flash, Anthropic launched Claude for Teachers, and Meta released a new open-source model. Meanwhile, tech CEOs lobbied Congress on biosecurity, and Google's new AI chief faces the challenge of catching OpenAI and Anthropic.

stories.title: Google's new AI boss faces a race to catch OpenAI and Anthropic
stories.why_it_matters: Google has installed a new head of AI as it scrambles to close the gap on rivals OpenAI (maker of ChatGPT) and Anthropic (maker of Claude). The new boss inherits a company that has enormous AI resources — the Gemini model family, DeepMind, and vast cloud infrastructure — but has repeatedly been seen as playing catch-up on the consumer AI side. For your GOOG holding, this is relevant: the pressure to compete is intense, but Google's scale means it remains a major player. The appointment signals urgency at the top.

stories.title: Google launches Gemini 3.7 Flash to rival Meta's new AI models
stories.why_it_matters: Google released Gemini 3.7 Flash this week — a faster, cheaper version of its Gemini AI model designed to go head-to-head with Meta's newly released open-source models. Separately, benchmarks show Google's Gemini 3.5 Flash model scoring just 2 points below Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.7 at about one-third of the cost. For everyday users, this means increasingly capable AI tools are getting dramatically cheaper. For GOOG investors, the competitive AI model race is producing real products, not just promises.

stories.title: Anthropic launches 'Claude for Teachers' as AI invades classrooms
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic has unveiled 'Claude for Teachers' — a specialised version of its Claude AI assistant built specifically for classroom use, joining OpenAI and Google who have both already launched education-focused AI tools. Teachers can use it to create lesson plans, grade work, and generate educational content. This is the AI companies' big push into education, a sector that will shape how the next generation learns. For parents and educators, it's both an exciting tool and a prompt to think about how AI is changing learning.

stories.title: Big Tech CEOs ask Congress to mandate synthetic DNA screening
stories.why_it_matters: The CEOs of OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft jointly appeared before the US Congress to request that the government mandate screening of synthetic DNA orders — a biosecurity measure designed to stop bad actors from using AI to design dangerous pathogens or bioweapons. It's a rare moment of agreement between fierce competitors, and it signals just how seriously the AI industry itself takes the risks of its own technology. Congress now has to decide whether to legislate this safeguard.

stories.title: Zuckerberg pushes 'superintelligent' AI for all as Meta drops new open-source model
stories.why_it_matters: Mark Zuckerberg announced that Meta's mission is now to make 'superintelligent' AI available to everyone, releasing a new open-source AI model that anyone can download and run for free. Open-source means companies and developers can modify and use the model without paying Meta — putting serious competitive pressure on the paid AI services from OpenAI and Anthropic. For everyday people, it means powerful AI tools could soon be freely available. For your GXAI.AX ETF, it's a reminder that the AI landscape is moving fast and competition is fierce.

sport.summary: NRL Round 24 kicks off tomorrow night with Panthers vs Roosters at CommBank Stadium. Big team news this week includes Brian To'o heading to PNG and Daly Cherry-Evans linked to Hull FC in England. AFL trade season is heating up with the Nick Butters saga threatening to reshape the draft.

stories.title: Four-way finals fight: Bulldogs' season on the brink heading into Round 24
stories.why_it_matters: With Round 24 starting tomorrow, the NRL finals race is going down to the wire. Fox Sports reports a four-team battle for the final spots, with the Bulldogs' season hanging in the balance. There's also a twist in the race for the minor premiership (finishing top of the ladder), with the top two not yet locked in. Round 24 shapes as one of the most consequential rounds of the season — Gold Coast Titans play the Knights on Sunday at 2pm.

stories.title: Brian To'o signs with PNG — and there's a rule-breaking twist
stories.why_it_matters: Panthers and Kangaroos winger Brian To'o has signed with the PNG Hunters franchise — but the deal has a controversial catch. The NRL apparently allowed PNG to break an existing rule to get the signing over the line, which has raised eyebrows about whether the league is applying rules consistently. To'o is a four-time premiership winner with Penrith, making him one of the biggest names to make the move to the expanded competition. His signing is a huge boost for PNG rugby league.

stories.title: Daly Cherry-Evans in 'advanced discussions' with Hull FC in England
stories.why_it_matters: Manly Sea Eagles captain and Australian halfback Daly Cherry-Evans is reportedly in advanced discussions to join Hull FC in the English Super League. At 37, DCE is in the twilight of his career and would be following a path taken by other NRL veterans heading to England. His departure would be a major blow for Manly — he's been their on-field leader for over a decade. Manly play the Dolphins this Friday at 4 Pines Park in what could be one of his last games in the competition.

stories.title: AFL: Nick Butters trade saga could reshape Pick 1 and the entire draft
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL trade period is still months away but the Nick Butters saga is already dominating footy media. The article suggests his trade from one club could have a domino effect that scrambles Pick 1 and reshapes the entire national draft. Without full article text, the specific details are limited — but if you follow AFL, this is the big trade story to watch heading into the off-season.
